## Modeling

Now, we will progress to the modeling section, where I will try to use two methods to predict the 6th man of the year (logistic regression and random forests). We will apply the best performing model to make our final prediction for who will win 6th man of the year in 2026.

### Train Test Split

```{r train_test_split}

train_index <- caret::createDataPartition(
  y = (smoy_data_full$smoy_winner), 
  p = 0.8,
  list = FALSE 
)

smoy_train <- smoy_data_full[train_index, ] %>% select(mpg, ppg, rpg, apg, ts, ftr, games_played, games_started, start_pct, team_win_pct, smoy_winner)
smoy_test <- smoy_data_full[-train_index, ] %>% select(mpg, ppg, rpg, apg, ts, ftr, games_played, games_started, start_pct, team_win_pct, smoy_winner)



train_index2009 <- caret::createDataPartition(
  y = (smoy_data_full_2009$smoy_winner), 
  p = 0.8,
  list = FALSE 
)

smoy_train_2009 <- smoy_data_full_2009[train_index2009, ] %>% select(mpg, ppg, rpg, apg, ts, ftr, games_played, games_started, start_pct, plus_minus, team_win_pct, games_played_pct, smoy_winner)
smoy_test_2009 <- smoy_data_full_2009[-train_index2009, ] %>% select(mpg, ppg, rpg, apg, ts, ftr, games_played, games_started, start_pct, plus_minus, team_win_pct, games_played_pct, smoy_winner)


```

### Logistic Regression

I will use forward selection to minimize AIC

```{r logistic_model}
log_model_null <- glm(smoy_winner ~ 1, 
    data = smoy_data_full, 
    family = "binomial")

# MASS::stepAIC(log_model_null, scope = ~ mpg + ppg + rpg + apg + ts + ftr + games_played + start_pct + team_win_pct, direction = "forward")

 log_model_aic <- glm(formula = smoy_winner ~ ppg + start_pct + team_win_pct + 
    games_played, family = "binomial", data = smoy_data_full)
 
 summary(log_model_aic)
 
 car::vif(log_model_aic)
 #vifs are good!
 
 #evaluate performance using k-fold cross-validation
 
 cv.glm(smoy_data_full, log_model_aic, K = 5)$delta[1]
 
 #great!! 
 
 smoy_pred_log <- smoy26 %>% select(athlete_display_name) %>% 
  mutate(smoy_pred_value = round(predict(log_model_aic,newdata=smoy26, type = "response"), 4))%>% 
  arrange(desc(smoy_pred_value))
 
 #all values are very low likely due to class imbalance

 
```

### Random Forest

We will evaluate performance of the models based on validation set accuracy while understanding biases towards class imbalance.

```{r randomForest}

smoy_rf_class <- randomForest(factor(smoy_winner) ~  ppg + start_pct + team_win_pct + 
    games_played, data = smoy_train, mtry = 3, ntree = 1000, importance = T)


smoy_accuracy  <- predict(smoy_rf_class,newdata=smoy_test, type = "class")

table(smoy_accuracy,smoy_test$smoy_winner) 
#high accuracy, but only predicting one true winner

```

### Random Forests considering Plus Minus (2009-2025)

#### Dealing with Class Imbalance

As only one player wins 6th man of the year every season, the dataset of all possible players will be extremely imbalanced. Here, I will try to address this in a couple ways.

##### Using Class Weights:

##### (<http://geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/how-to-calculate-class-weights-for-random-forests-in-r/>)

```{r class_imbalance_rf}
smoy_counts <- table(smoy_train$smoy_winner)
smoy_weights <- 1 / smoy_counts
smoy_weights_normalized <- smoy_weights / min(smoy_weights)

smoy_weights2009 <- 1 / smoy_counts2009
smoy_weights_normalized2009 <- smoy_weights2009 / min(smoy_weights2009)


smoy_rf_classwt <- randomForest(factor(smoy_winner) ~  ppg + start_pct + team_win_pct + 
    games_played, data = smoy_train, mtry = 3, ntree = 1000, classwt = smoy_weights_normalized, importance = T)

#predicting one true winner

    games_played_pct + plus_minus, data = smoy_train_2009, mtry = 3, ntree = 1000,  classwt = smoy_weights_normalized2009, importance = T)


smoy_accuracy_classwt2009 <- predict(smoy_rf_classwt2009, newdata = smoy_test_2009, type = "class")

#improvement, still very high accuracy

#I am okay with using this model as it was good in identification of winners as we only picked up one false positives
```
